source_snapshot.procedure: Select Operations > Factory Reset and reset BMC and server settings; generic setup says clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Factory reset without error; BMC returns to default settings including server settings, accounts/passwords, policies, LDAP, network addresses and time.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes a preliminary cold reset, five-second wait and unverified generic Redfish `FactoryReset` with `curl -k` and exposed credentials; it cannot prove supported action, destructive scope, defaults or recovery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly rejects that sequence and requires vendor scope/defaults, secure baseline, one approved action, independent bootstrap/recovery and complete comparison before reconfiguration.

old_problem: Factory reset is not a generic Manager.Reset type and may erase the very accounts, IP/VLAN, certificates, directory, time and audit paths needed to observe recovery. The source does not define version-specific BMC/server scope, preserved exceptions or defaults, while the proposed cold-reset-plus-Redfish sequence can strand access and destroy valid default-state evidence.
disposition_reason: Retain the destructive Operations > Factory Reset coverage, but gate it on a firmware-specific vendor action/scope/default matrix, secure pre-reset export, independent physical/discovery/bootstrap access and one point-of-action approval. Compare every default before any reconfiguration and stop without retry on scope/recovery failure. These Project/vendor bindings make execution NOT READY when absent; the Review decision itself is complete.
decision_basis: XLSX row 912, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, ordinary reboot and other operations history, and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.
A cold BMC reboot is not a factory reset, and a generic Redfish ResetType cannot be assumed supported or equivalent to the source WebUI action.
The source explicitly lists destructive configuration domains, so evidence and recovery must be established before their loss and post-reset defaults must be captured before restoration.
ED-03 prohibits guessed OEM/API parameters, ED-17 preserves logs before deletion/loss, ED-20 preserves WebUI factory-reset coverage and ED-30/V3.1 one-shot controls prohibit automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify one approved WebUI BMC factory reset against a complete authoritative default matrix
test_case.purpose: Verify one vendor-supported BMC WebUI factory-reset action restores every in-scope BMC and server setting to its authoritative firmware/Project default, removes the intended custom access/configuration only, preserves documented exceptions, leaves host behavior within the approved scope and permits secure controlled recovery before reconfiguration.
required_package: BMC/SUT asset, MAC/serial, firmware/build/active bank, host power/OS state and current network/access identity
Vendor documentation for exact Operations > Factory Reset control, BMC/server scope, preserved exceptions and expected reset/host-power behavior

Authoritative default matrix for accounts/roles/password bootstrap, policies, LDAP/RADIUS, network/VLAN, time/NTP, certificates, alerting, thresholds, boot/server settings and every additional scoped field
Secure redacted configuration export/hash and preserved pre-reset audit/SEL evidence with secret/volatile handling
Factory DHCP/default-IP/discovery and approved initial-account or zero-touch provisioning procedure
Independent physical/console recovery owner, vendor escalation, staged recovery deadlines and non-return procedure
Maintenance/destructive approval, no-conflicting-operation proof and separately authorized post-verdict reconfiguration plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL DESTRUCTIVE; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVAL. Preserve logs and securely export/hash all scoped settings before loss. Independently verify target asset, exact vendor WebUI factory-reset control/scope/default matrix, bootstrap/recovery access and absence of firmware/config/KVM/SOL/virtual-media/power/critical-host work. A human invokes the supported WebUI action once—no preliminary cold reset, generic Redfish guess or fallback retry. From the independent path, timestamp disconnect, network/discovery, service, bootstrap/authentication and full-sensor recovery. Before restoring anything, compare every scoped setting with the authoritative default/preserved-exception matrix and confirm host/server impact. Preserve verdict evidence; reconfigure only after separate owner authorization.
test_case.expected_result: One approved action produces the documented factory-reset audit and recovery sequence. Every scoped BMC/server field equals its version-specific default, every documented exception remains as specified, prior accounts/passwords/policies/directory/network/time/certificate/threshold/boot customizations are removed exactly as intended, identity/firmware and host state follow the approved scope, secure bootstrap succeeds and complete management/sensor health returns within deadlines. Default-state evidence exists before reconfiguration.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact vendor action/scope evidence, secure baseline, single-action proof, independent recovery/bootstrap, complete default/exemption comparison, expected host impact and engineer verdict before reconfiguration. Ping, HTTP status, `mc info`, a cold reset or partial settings check cannot pass. Unsupported action, wrong scope, missed deadline, insecure/unavailable bootstrap, unexpected retained/lost field, identity/host impact mismatch or incomplete sensors is FAIL and stops the run. Missing defaults, secure export, recovery or destructive approval is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Treat the action as CRITICAL and destructive; independently verify asset/MAC/serial/firmware/host state immediately before approval.
Do not clear logs; export configuration, audit/SEL and recovery artifacts because reset may erase them.
Do not run the source cold-reset plus generic `FactoryReset`, use `curl -k`, expose credentials or guess an OEM/Redfish action/value.
Confirm physical/discovery/bootstrap recovery and ownership before losing accounts, addresses, certificates and directory authentication.
Execute one WebUI factory reset only; no preliminary reset, power cycle, guessed fallback or automatic retry. Record defaults before any restore.
expected_evidence: Approval/change record, target asset/MAC/serial/firmware/host state, vendor action/scope reference and no-conflicting-operation checklist
Secure redacted configuration export/hash and complete pre-reset matrix for all scoped settings plus preserved audit/SEL
WebUI action screenshots/audit, single-action proof and staged disconnect/network/discovery/service/bootstrap/auth/sensor recovery timeline
Post-reset identity/firmware/host state and complete default/preserved-exception comparison with volatile/secret distinctions
Physical/discovery/bootstrap recovery proof, no retry/insecure credential use and evidence captured before reconfiguration
Final BMC/SUT health, approved reconfiguration boundary and engineer-owned verdict
test_case.recovery: If target, scope, bootstrap or recovery is wrong, do not repeat the reset or power-cycle. Use the pre-arranged physical/console/default-discovery path, preserve audit/SEL and first-failure evidence and escalate to the BMC owner/vendor. Restore configuration only from the approved secure export after identity and access are verified and the default-state verdict evidence is complete; every restoration is a separate authorized action.

source_conflict.reason: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require BMC plus in-scope server factory defaults. Exact action, scope and default values are critical Project/vendor readiness inputs rather than contradictory purposes.

blocked.reason: The destructive objective, evidence, one-shot safety and recovery are fully defined. Execution waits for vendor scope/defaults, secure baseline and independent recovery.
